title: Check yourself: The usage policy and sensitive data

questions.stem: An HR coordinator wants Claude to summarise survey comments by department. The comments include employees' names and health details, and policy restricts regulated personal data. Which step fits?

options.text: Upload the comments unchanged and tell Claude to leave all names out of the summary
options.says: Ruled out because asking Claude to leave names out "is a request, and it does not satisfy a policy control".

options.text: Get a manager's approval and upload the file to a tool the team already likes
options.says: Ruled out because the organisation's policy "decides which tools and data are permitted at work", and a manager's liking for a tool does not change that.

options.text: Swap each name for a code and treat the file as anonymous
options.says: Ruled out because "Pseudonymised data is still personal data under many rules, because the key can reverse it".

options.text: Redact identifiers and clinical specifics, keep the grouping, then check the output
options.says: The task can proceed if the data changes: remove identifiers and sensitive specifics, keep what the summary needs, then check for re-identification.

questions.stem: A team uses Claude to draft decision letters about loan applications that go straight to applicants. Under the Usage Policy which pair of safeguards applies to this use?

options.text: A qualified reviewer before sending, and disclosure that AI helped
options.says: Financial decisions that affect individuals are high-risk: a qualified professional reviews them and recipients are told AI helped.

options.text: A confidentiality footer on each letter, and a monthly accuracy count
options.says: Ruled out because the requirement is that you "disclose that AI helped produce it, at a minimum at the beginning of each session", which a footer and a count do not provide.

options.text: A second model's approval of each letter, and removal of applicants' names
options.says: Ruled out because the reviewer must be a "qualified professional in the field", and a second model is not one.

options.text: A legal sign-off once a year, and a note in the privacy policy
options.says: Ruled out because the review must happen "before it is disseminated or finalised", not once a year.

questions.stem: A consultant says: "These sales figures are for internal analysis only, so the customer identities can stay in the file." The analyst must compare purchases across two years, and policy restricts regulated personal data. What is the best response?

options.text: Swap each name for a code, keep the codes in the file, and then call the data anonymous
options.says: Ruled out because "Pseudonymised data is still personal data under many rules, because the key can reverse it".

options.text: Keep the file as it is, since internal analysis lowers the data's class to internal
options.says: Ruled out because "internal use does not change the class of the data".

options.text: Aggregate to totals per segment and per period, then remove names and account numbers
options.says: Aggregation is the strongest technique, the comparison needs trends and not rows, and the class is set by the data.

options.text: Keep the file and ask Claude not to retain the figures after the session ends
options.says: Ruled out because asking Claude not to retain the file "is a request, and it does not satisfy a policy control".
